rubric.source: Severity weighting and minimal-type-set principles adapted from MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics), MQM Council, CC BY 4.0 — https://www.themqm.org/mqm-pillars/typology and https://www.themqm.org/mqm-pillars/the-mqm-scoring-models

error_types.note: placeholder lost or mutated; delimiter or environment imbalance
em-dash house rule and similar style punctuation

rubric.scoring: Errors counted against the skill: (a) planted corpus errors left unfixed, (b) new errors introduced in the polished text (any markup mutation counts critical), (c) unjustified claim inflation. Penalty = sum(severity weights) / (words / 100); TQ = 100 - Penalty; regression threshold TQ >= 95.
principles: minimal type set — score only the seven types above, nothing else
each error is counted once, at its highest applicable severity
hierarchy first — when two types could both apply, the lower dimension number wins

corpus.passage: In order to solve the empty container repositioning problem, we propose a two-stage heuristic---the master stage assigns vessels and the local stage repositions containers. Extensive experiments shows that our method achieves good results. It can be seen that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods (see \cite{song2023empty} for the problem setting), and the average cost reduction is reported in Table \ref{tab:results}.

annotations.expected_fix: replace em-dash with a colon or restructure the sentence
state the measured metric, e.g. achieves an average cost reduction of 3.2%
extracted as a placeholder, returned verbatim
extracted as a placeholder, returned verbatim

corpus.passage: We test the proposed algorithm on 20 randomly generated instances. The algorithm achieves an average optimality gap of 0.0%, and our method works well under all settings.

annotations.expected_fix: achieved — past tense for experimental results
scope the claim to the tested settings (no-inflate rule)

corpus.passage: We apply Benders decomposition to the two-stage model. This method converges in a finite number of iterations. The proposed approach is also effective. It solves instances with up to 200 nodes within minutes.

annotations.span: This method / The proposed approach / It
annotations.expected_fix: resolve the reference chain to one consistent, specific reference such as 'The decomposition algorithm'
quantify or merge into the adjacent sentence

corpus.passage:
The total cost is
\[ C = \sum_{i \in V} c_i x_i + \sum_{j \in W} f_j y_j \]
where $c_i$ and $f_j$ denotes the unit costs. Preliminary results shows that the model reduces the total cost by 12% (see Figure \ref{fig:convergence}).

annotations.expected_fix: all extracted as placeholders and returned verbatim; display-math delimiters balanced

evals.prompt: polish the abstract section in els-cas-templates/manuscript.tex
evals.expected_output: Should improve grammar, tighten academic tone, fix vague language in the abstract while every LaTeX island (\textyen{}, $K=2$, \textit{}, \cite, \ref) round-trips verbatim. Changes presented as severity-grouped numbered hunks ([critical|grammar] etc.); after edits, report the post-edit verification trio (em-dash grep, round-trip check, delimiter check); paragraph scale or larger triggers the jargon-check follow-up.

evals.prompt: 帮我润色这段话（corpus c1）：In order to solve the empty container repositioning problem, we propose a two-stage heuristic---the master stage assigns vessels and the local stage repositions containers. Extensive experiments shows that our method achieves good results. It can be seen that the proposed approach outperforms the baseline methods (see \cite{song2023empty} for the problem setting), and the average cost reduction is reported in Table \ref{tab:results}.
evals.expected_output: Pasted-text path: severity-grouped numbered Changes + a round-trip check line + clean Polished version; no Edit tool use. All annotations of c1 fixed per their expected_fix; \cite and \ref return verbatim.

evals.prompt: polish the file els-cas-templates/manuscript.tex, just grammar check
evals.expected_output: Should only apply dimension 1 (critical-severity grammar hunks) and ask the user whether a full polish is wanted. Should NOT rewrite for tone or conciseness.

evals.prompt: polish this passage (corpus c4, contains display math and inline math)
evals.expected_output: Display equation \[...\], inline $c_i$/$f_j$, and \ref{fig:convergence} extracted as numbered placeholders before rewriting and returned verbatim; round-trip check reported; 'denotes'→'denote', 'shows'→'show'; no edit inside the math environments.

evals.prompt: polish this passage (corpus c2, results reporting)
evals.expected_output: 'achieves'→'achieved' (past tense); 'works well' quantified or deleted; 'under all settings' scoped to tested settings per the no-inflate rule; no severity inflation of the 0.0% gap claim.

evals.prompt: regression: score the output of eval 2 with the rubric and report TQ
evals.expected_output: Penalty computed from unfixed planted errors and newly introduced errors using weights minor=1/major=5/critical=25 per 100 words; TQ = 100 - Penalty; TQ >= 95 passes; a mutated \cite would alone cost 25 (critical).
